sentences.text: JODHPUR  S.B. Criminal Miscellaneous Bail Application No. 15127/2022 Mukesh Kumar S/o Mohan Lal, Aged About 22 Years, Deva Ji Ka Gura, P.s. Amet, Dist. Rajsamand (Raj.).

(At Present Petitioner Is Lodged In Dist. Jail, Rajsamand).
 ----Petitione  Versus 1. State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp 2. Khushaboo D/o Jethu Singh, Aged About 19 Years, Deva  Ji Ka Gura, Amet, Dist. Rajsamand (Raj.).
----Respondents For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Rajendra Singh Rathore
For Respondent(s) : Mr. MA Siddiqui AAG
Mr. Vikram Singh
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MADAN GOPAL VYAS Order 21/04/2023

The present criminal misc. bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. has been preferred by the petitioner in connection with FIR no.274/2022, Police Station Amet, District Rajsamand lodged for the offences under Sections 376(2)(n), 376D, 384 of the IPC and under Section 3/4, 5(G)(I)/6 of the POCSO Act.
Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has falsely been implicated in the present case.
It is submitted that the present FIR has been lodged after inordinate delay and only to counter-blast the FIR No.272/2022 lodged at Police Station Amet, District Rajsamand by the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed that the petitioner may be enlarged on bail.
] Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel appearing for the complainant opposed the prayer made by learned counsel for the petitioner.

sentences.text: Learned Public Prosecutor submits that in the statement of victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., the victim has specifically levelled allegations against the present petitioner.
It is further submitted that in the present case, the statements of witnesses are yet to be recorded.
Learned Public Prosecutor further submits that in the present case, the allegations of gang rape has been made and, therefore, the petitioner may not be enlarged on bail.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, after perusing the statement of victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. and looking to the gravity of the offence, without commenting on the merits and demerits of the case, I do not find it to be a fit case for grant of bail.
The bail application is therefore, rejected.
However, the learned trial court is directed to expedite the trial of the case.
A copy of this order be sent to the trial court by email or by FAX.

(MADAN GOPAL VYAS),J 100-CPGoyal/-
